key_terms.meaning: A bar that carries loads applied across its axis (transverse loads), so it bends rather than only stretches
A beam resting on a pin support at one end and a roller support at the other; both ends can rotate freely
A beam fixed at one end and completely free at the other
A beam whose ends extend past one or both supports
A support that stops both translation and rotation, so it gives two reaction forces and one reaction moment
A support that gives only one reaction force, perpendicular to the surface it rolls on
A load acting at a single section, measured in N or kN; W denotes its value
A load spread evenly along the beam, w N/m (or kN/m), so the total load is w × L over length L
A pure moment applied at a point on the beam, measured in N·m; it changes the bending moment but not the shear force
A sketch of the beam alone, with every support replaced by its reaction forces and every load shown in its true position
ΣFx = 0, ΣFy = 0, ΣM = 0 about any point; for a plane beam they give up to three unknown reactions
The force across a section of the beam, equal to the algebraic sum of all transverse forces on one side of the section
The moment about a section of the beam, equal to the algebraic sum of moments of all forces on one side about that section
Sagging (beam bends like a smile) is taken as positive bending moment; upward force on the left face of the cut is positive shear
A section where the bending moment is zero and changes sign, so the beam changes from sagging to hogging
Negative bending moment that makes the beam curve like a frown, tension appearing in the top fibres
dV/dx = −w, where w is the downward distributed load in N/m; a UDL therefore gives a straight sloping shear line
dM/dx = V, so the shear force equals the slope of the BM curve and V = 0 marks a maximum or minimum M

takeaways: Every real beam problem starts by drawing the free body diagram: replace each support with the reactions it can give, then solve ΣFx = 0, ΣFy = 0, ΣM = 0.
A pin or roller gives one vertical reaction each; a fixed end gives a vertical reaction and a moment, which makes a cantilever solvable from the free end.
The shear force at a section is the running sum of all transverse forces to one side of that section; the bending moment is the running sum of their moments.
Shear force changes by jumps at point loads and by a straight-line slope under a UDL; the bending moment curve is one order smoother than the shear curve.
The bending moment is maximum where the shear force is zero, or where a point load acts, or at a fixed end.
In an overhanging beam part of the span is hogging, so the bending moment diagram crosses zero at a point of contraflexure.
dM/dx = V and dV/dx = −w let you build the second diagram from the area under the first without writing every equation.
An applied couple produces a sudden jump in the bending moment diagram but leaves the shear force diagram unchanged.
bank_note: Long answers here are almost always a full worked solution: draw the FBD, find the reactions, then draw the shear force and bending moment diagrams with every value and zero-crossing marked — some syllabi add the load–shear–moment differential relations and the sign convention as a short theory part.

bank.q: Classify beams by the way they are supported. Explain simply supported, cantilever, overhanging, fixed and continuous beams, and state which reactions each support type provides.
outline: Definition of a beam as a bar under transverse loading
Pin, roller and fixed supports with the reaction components each gives
Simply supported: one pin, one roller, both ends free to rotate
Cantilever: one fixed end, free end, three reactions
Overhanging: span plus one or both ends projecting beyond supports
Fixed and continuous beams as statically indeterminate cases

bank.q: Explain the sign convention used for shear force and bending moment in beam diagrams, and state why a single consistent convention is necessary.
outline: Left-hand face: upward force on left piece is positive shear
Sagging moment taken positive, hogging negative
Effect of sign on the shape of the BMD and on the tension face
Consistency needed so the section values from either side of the cut agree

bank.q: State and explain the relations dV/dx = −w and dM/dx = V. Show what each relation implies about the shape of the shear and bending moment diagrams for a UDL, a point load and a couple.
outline: Derivation from a small element of length dx
UDL: shear linear, moment parabolic
Point load: shear jumps, moment has a kink
Couple: moment jumps, shear unaffected
Zero shear locates maximum moment

bank.q: Define shear force and bending moment at a section of a beam. Write the steps used to draw the SFD and BMD for a statically determinate beam.
outline: Shear force as algebraic sum of transverse forces on one side
Bending moment as algebraic sum of moments on one side
Steps: FBD, reactions, sections, expressions, plot, mark maximum values

bank.q: A cantilever of length 4 m is fixed at the left end. It carries a point load of 10 kN at the free end and a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Draw the SFD and BMD and find the maximum values.
outline: Reactions: vertical 26 kN upward and fixing moment 64 kN·m at the fixed end
Shear steps from 26 kN at fixed end to 0 at free end, straight line under UDL, step of 10 kN at the tip
BM zero at free end, parabolic under UDL, ends at −64 kN·m at the fixed end
Maximum sagging-negative values stated with sign

bank.q: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m over the whole span plus a point load of 20 kN at 2 m from the left support. Draw the SFD and BMD and locate the maximum bending moment.
outline: Reactions from moments about each support
Shear diagram: sloping line with a jump at the point load
Zero-shear section located between the supports
Maximum BM computed at the zero-shear section
Parabolic and linear portions drawn with values at ends and under the load

bank.q: A simply supported beam of span L carries a UDL w per unit length and also a clockwise couple M₀ at the mid-span. Derive and sketch the SFD and BMD, and state the effect of the couple on each diagram.
outline: Reactions from ΣM about supports
Shear diagram: straight sloping lines, no jump from the couple
Bending moment diagram: parabolic, sudden jump of M₀ at mid-span
Position of maximum BM found by setting V = 0

bank.q: An overhanging beam of span 8 m between supports carries a UDL of 3 kN/m over its whole length and overhangs 2 m beyond the right support with a point load of 15 kN at the free end. Draw the SFD and BMD and find the point of contraflexure.
outline: Reactions from moment equilibrium
Hogging moment in the overhang, sagging between supports
Locate zero moment between the supports by solving the quadratic
State the contraflexure distance from a support
Mark maximum positive moment where shear is zero

bank.q: A cantilever 3 m long carries a UDL of 6 kN/m from the fixed end for 2 m and a point load of 12 kN at the free end. Draw the SFD and BMD, and state the maximum bending moment.
outline: Fixed-end reaction and fixing moment
Shear diagram: two straight portions and a step
Bending moment: parabolic over the loaded part, linear beyond
Maximum BM at the fixed end with sign

bank.q: Using only the relations dV/dx = −w and dM/dx = V, find the change in bending moment between two sections from the area of the shear diagram between them. Verify the result for a simply supported beam under a UDL over the whole span.
outline: ΔV = area under load curve with sign
ΔM = area under shear curve
Apply to the simply supported UDL case and obtain wL²/8 at mid-span
Explain why the maximum moment lies at zero shear

bank.q: Compare the bending moment diagrams of a simply supported beam and a cantilever of the same span carrying the same UDL. Explain the difference in maximum moment values and in the shape of the curves, and say which arrangement uses the material better.
outline: Simply supported: end moments zero, maximum wL²/8 at mid-span
Cantilever: maximum wL²/2 at fixed end, zero at the free end
Curve shape and tension face discussion
Simply supported beam needs a smaller section for the same load

bank.q: For an overhanging beam, explain why the bending moment changes sign within the span. Discuss where the contraflexure point lies for different overhang lengths and what it means for the reinforcement or section design.
outline: Hogging over the support near the overhang, sagging inside the span
Sign change located by setting M = 0
Contraflexure moves as overhang length grows
Tension face swaps, so steel in a concrete beam must be placed on both faces

bank.q: A beam is loaded such that the shear force diagram crosses zero at three sections. Comment on the number of possible maximum bending moments, and explain how you would decide the design moment without plotting the whole diagram.
outline: Each zero-shear section is a local maximum or minimum of M
Use ΔM = area under V between successive points
Absolute value of M controls design, sign decides the tension face
Comparison of candidate values to pick the governing moment

bank.q: Explain why support reactions must be found before drawing SFD and BMD, and discuss what changes when one end of a beam is fixed instead of simply supported.
outline: Reactions enter every section expression
Fixed end adds a reaction moment, making the beam statically indeterminate when combined with other supports
Statically determinate cases and the extra compatibility condition needed otherwise
Effect on the shape of the BMD near the fixed end

glossary.def: A structural bar that carries loads applied perpendicular to its length and resists them mainly by bending.
The horizontal distance between two adjacent supports of a beam.
A beam fixed at one end, with the other end free to deflect.
A beam with a pin support at one end and a roller support at the other, giving two vertical reactions only.
A beam that extends beyond one or both of its supports.
A beam with both ends built in, so no rotation is possible at either end.
A single beam running over more than two supports.
A cantilever with an added simple support at some point along its length.
A hinge-type support that prevents translation but allows rotation, giving two reaction components.
A support that gives one reaction force normal to the rolling surface and allows free rotation.
A concentrated force acting at a single section of a beam, measured in N or kN.
A load of constant intensity w Newton per metre spread along a length of the beam.
A pure moment of magnitude M₀ applied at one section of a beam, measured in N·m.
A diagram of the beam alone with all supports replaced by reaction forces and all loads shown in position.
The force or moment that a support exerts on the beam to keep it in equilibrium.
The internal transverse force at a section, equal to the algebraic sum of all forces on one side of that section.
The internal moment at a section, equal to the algebraic sum of the moments of all forces on one side about that section.
A positive bending moment that makes the beam concave upward, producing tension in the bottom fibres.
A negative bending moment that makes the beam concave downward, producing tension in the top fibres.
A section of a beam where the bending moment is zero and changes sign.
A section where the shear force is zero, marking a maximum or minimum on the bending moment diagram.
A beam whose support reactions can be found from the three equations of equilibrium alone.
